 Judgment

This appeal filed by the appellant KSRTC under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V. Act') challenging the quantum of award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Belur, Hassan in MVC No.588/2018 dated 29.06.2022.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent.
3.
The rank of the parties before Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.
4. The case of the petitioner (respondent) is that the petitioner was traveling in the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-18-F-691 on 25.06.2016 along with his friend.

At about 3.45 a.m., when they reached near Mallikarjunapura Village, the driver of the said Bus has driven the Bus in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and taken the bus to the left side of the road, due to which,
the Bus toppled down to its left side.

Due to the impact of the said accident, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he was admitted to the hospital, NC: 2024:KHC:20339 treated as inpatient, spent lot of amount towards medical expenses.
Due to the injury, he suffered the fracture of upper limb as well as L-1 Vertebral and he was unable to do the work.
Hence, he has filed the petition.
5. In response to the summons, the respondent- KSRTC appeared and filed statement of objections denying the rash and negligent driving as well as age, income, occupation of the petitioner.
As such prayed for dismissal the claim petition.

6. Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
"1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 25.06.2016 at above 3.45 a.m., near Mallikarjunapura Village, when petitioner was proceeding traveling in KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-18-F-691, the driver of above said bus by its driving in a rash and negligent manner lost control over it and consequently the bus was toppled down to left side of the road and thereby, petitioner was sustained grievous injuries on all the parts of the body as contended by him?
Whether the petitioner is entitled from the respondent?
If so, how much?

Divisional Controller vs Venkateshchari on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105425411/
2 3.
What order or award?"

7. In order to prove the case of the claimant, the petitioner himself examined as P.W.1, also examined the doctor as P.W.2 and got marked 11 documents and also on behalf of the respondent,
examined RW.1 and marked Ex.R-1.
8.

After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.4,90,975/- on various heads which are as under:
1. Towards Pain and Suffering Rs.40,000-00 2.

Medical expenses Rs.17,655-00 3. Conveyance, Attendant, Diet Food & Rs.10,000-00 Miscellaneous expenses 4. Loss of income during treatment Rs.9,500-00 period 5. Loss of future income due to disability Rs.4,13,820-00 Total Rs.4,90,975-00 9.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the KSRTC filed this appeal by challenging the quantum of award of compensation on the ground that it is exorbitant and excessive.
Learned counsel for the appellant has contended that the doctor-P.W.2 who examined by petitioner was not a treated doctor.
The doctor has opined that the petitioner has permanent disability of 30% to the whole body is not correct.
Normally, 1/3 required to be taken as disability amount and future prospects considered by Tribunal which is also not correct.

The disability itself has not been properly stated by the Tribunal, such being the case, question of granting 30%
disability does not arises.
Hence, prayed for allowing the appeal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent supported the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and contended that the award amount passed by Tribunal by computing each amount is just and proper and no need to interfere and prayed for dismissing the petition.

12. After hearing the arguments and on perusal of the records, the point that arise from my consideration is:
"Whether the Tribunal considered the disability as 30% to the whole body is excessive and considered 10% future prospects is required which call for interference?
NC: 2024:KHC:20339 Divisional Controller vs Venkateshchari on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105425411/
3 13.

On perusal of the records, the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 reveals that the petitioner while he was traveling in the KSRTC Bus on 25.06.2016 along with his friend, at about 3.45 a.m., the driver of the said Bus has driven the Bus in a high speed in rash and negligent manner and taken the bus to the left side of the road, due to which, the Bus toppled down to its left side.

Due to the impact of the said accident, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries near vertebrae lumbar region and the doctor P.W.2-Dr.Ramakrishna Bhat who has issued the disability certificate and has opined that even after the accident, when the petitioner came for assessment of disability in the year 2021, the petitioner complained the pain in the right shoulder joint on lifting heavy weights and doing hard work, he complained pain in the mid back while sitting and standing for long time and walking for long distance and also complained pain on bending and lifting weights and also he is not in a position to do any hard manual work.
The doctor assessed the disability of 50% of L-1 vertebrae which is a compression for fracture and that is 30% to the body.

During the cross examination, it was adjusted that there is no problem for doing any light work and doing any business etc, but nothing elicited NC: 2024:KHC:20339 to disbelieving the evidence of the doctor.
L1 Vertebrae always bears the weight of the body, if it is a fracture, it is very for a man or a woman to walk long distance and bend or lifting any weight.
Such being the case, if 50% assessed by the Tribunal towards L-1 vertebrae is appropriate.
However, he has given 30% to the physical disability and not properly done the evidence and assessing 30% is not in accordance with the guidelines.
Such being the case, I am of the view, instead of taking 30%, if 25% disability is considered to the whole body, that will be appropriate.

14. As regards to the future prospects, the Tribunal assessed that this injury would cause future functional disability and medical jurisprudence also considered by the Tribunal that there is a chances of becoming bedridden on account of paralysis, paralysis of the lower limbs due to the L-1 vertebrae compression fracture.
Such being the case, definitely there will be functional disability of the injured claimant.
Therefore the Tribunal has assessed only 10% for future prospects and there is no need to interfere in the same.

If Rs.9,500/- per month is taken as notional income for the accident occurred in the year 2016,
that will be appropriate.

10% future prospects of Rs.9,500/- is Rs.950/- and Rs.9,500/- + Rs.950/-
it comes to Rs.10,450/-.
Therefore, the loss of future income due to disability comes to Rs.3,44,850/- (Rs.10,450x12x11x25%).
This would be the loss of income due to future disability, the same is reduced from Rs.4,13,820/-to Rs.3,44,820/-.

16. As regards to the pain and suffering, medical expenses, conveyance, loss of income, loss of income during the treatment period, the Tribunal has assessed properly, the same is not challenged by the respondent, such being the case, there is no need to interfere.
17. There is no need to interfere in the other heads or compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The appellant shall deposit the entire award amount within 60 days and if any amount deposited, the same shall be transmitted to the Tribunal;

(iv) Draw award accordingly;
 (v) The statutory amount is directed to be transmit to  the Tribunal.
